objective: Compare old and new first denoisers on receiver-generated queries, then compare complete candidate receivers for accuracy, convergence and measured runtime.
data_scope: Queries derived from the project's simulated AFDM observations, with multipath, multiuser interference and receiver feedback; no hardware-measured observations are available in the current comparison. No fresh additive noise is injected into saved queries.

execution.reason: This turn designs the comparison; no batch experiment or training launch is requested.
execution.implementation: Extend existing saved-query and closed-loop diagnostic runners in an independent candidate directory; preserve frozen model bindings.

weights.development: Freeze and hash a completed current EMA checkpoint; record its actual epoch. Do not evaluate a changing best checkpoint during one comparison.
weights.formal: Prefer the candidate selected by the existing validation-DSM rule after its scheduled 200 epochs, versus the frozen old epoch-200 model. Never select checkpoints on receiver test outcomes.
weights.interpretation: An interim candidate-versus-old comparison has unequal training budgets; neither shared-input nor closed-loop results isolate noise-model changes from all architecture changes.

common_controls.observations: Identical channel, pilot, activity, receive-noise realization, receiver initialization, normalization and noise estimate within each paired scene.
common_controls.phase: Known phase initially, consistent with the current SNR main experiment. Estimated-phase results, if later requested, are a separate comparison.
common_controls.formal_scene_ids: Existing 0-999 protocol; flag scenes already used in development. These reused scenes are not an unseen confirmation set.
common_controls.development: Reuse existing diagnostic scenes and -4/0 dB conditions to validate instrumentation and fix settings before a larger run; keep the failure-enriched group separate.
common_controls.truth: Only the scoring observer accesses true channels and activity. C estimation, mean/variance inference, decisions, parameter selection and online stopping do not access test truth.

methods: old first denoiser with its scalar variance
new first denoiser with public estimated C
shared_input_comparison.queries: Score every iteration online during diagnostic trajectory collection. Feed exactly the same query r to all methods; only the designated trajectory owner updates the receiver.
shared_input_comparison.trajectory_sources: Evaluate on trajectories generated by both old and new receivers, and report each source separately. The first query is common before denoiser feedback.
shared_input_comparison.purpose: Measures conditional-mean denoising on identical inputs; does not establish the shadow method's closed-loop convergence.
shared_input_comparison.raw_metric: Active-user NMSE = 10 log10(sum over scenes and true active users of ||D(r)-h||_F^2 / sum ||h||_F^2). Include missed active users; do not condition on correct detection.
shared_input_comparison.optional_covariance_ablation: If attributing benefit specifically to correlation shape, compare new C with new p_k I using exactly the same per-user power p_k=tr(C_k)/dimension; new global-vI versus per-user C also changes power.

closed_loop_comparison.development_controls: Retain new vI/C at 0.2 to isolate the effect of the 0.4 setting within each new interface. Do not repeat 0.6 in the main comparison unless new evidence motivates it; preserve its existing failures.
closed_loop_comparison.attribution: Old native receiver uses its trained second network; new receivers currently use a finite-difference variance interface. The classifier is frozen. This is a complete-interface comparison, not a pure first-network causal ablation.
closed_loop_comparison.diagnostic_fixed_horizon: Use the same fixed 120 iterations for all arms and record all iterates, including those after the original stop would trigger. If extending this horizon, choose the extension from development outcomes before formal evaluation.
closed_loop_comparison.native_stopping: Separately measure actual inference under the same currently used known-phase stopping settings: minimum 60, maximum 600, relative-change tolerance 0.0005 plus existing stability checks. Fixed-horizon traces and early-stopped deployment runs are different measurements.
closed_loop_comparison.failures: Keep all scenes, including divergence and nonfinite or unsupported queries. Report unavailable pooled raw NMSE explicitly rather than dropping failed scenes.

speed_and_timing.target_rule: Per scene, find the first window of ten consecutive iterations at or below a target. Report the window start and confirmation iteration (start+9), plus cumulative time at confirmation. This uses truth offline and is not an online stopping rule.
speed_and_timing.target_reporting: Report the fraction of all scenes attaining each target, right-censor nonattainment at the common budget, and show the full attainment curve. Do not compare only successful-scene mean iteration counts.
speed_and_timing.accuracy_cost_tradeoff: Compare NMSE at identical iteration and elapsed-time budgets and cost to identical NMSE targets. Do not infer speed from reaching each method's own, potentially inferior, plateau.
speed_and_timing.runtime_environment: Dedicated GPU measurement after scheduled training completes; same device, precision, batch size, warmup and comparable execution optimization. Rotate method order and use three timing repetitions per scene.
exclude_from_inference_time: one-time compilation or CUDA-graph setup reported separately
speed_and_timing.breakdown: Also report denoiser-only and mean-plus-variance module latency; end-to-end runtime includes the complete receiver computation.

analysis.aggregation: Pooled energy-ratio NMSE plus per-scene paired differences; do not average dB and call it pooled NMSE.
analysis.uncertainty: Paired bootstrap by scene with 95% intervals. All methods, users and iterations belonging to a resampled scene remain together; users and iterations are not independent repetitions.
outputs: shared-input NMSE versus query iteration by trajectory source
closed-loop raw and final-channel NMSE versus iteration
summary of median and tail runtime, stopping, failure and variance-floor rates
analysis.success_interpretation: Report separately whether the new mean is better on identical queries, whether its receiver reaches common accuracy sooner, and whether final accuracy and detection remain competitive. No single favorable curve substitutes for all three.
